text:
jess: Customer reporting 403 on API calls coming from a Vercel-hosted service worker in Safari. Happens only when using our TypeScript/browser SDK from inside the SW scope.

sam (devex): Can you paste the minimal repro steps and SDK version? Safari specific is interesting.

jess: Repro steps from customer:
1) Deploy a small Vercel app with a service worker that proxies requests to /api/proxy -> forwards to our hosted API.
2) Client (page) calls the SW which does fetch('/api/proxy', {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`}})
3) In Safari 16.4/16.5, the OPTIONS preflight returns 200 but browser still blocks the actual request and the console shows "Request header field Authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers" then main request gets 403 from our backend.

They included the SDK call they actually used (weirdly they use our fetch wrapper in the edge bundle):

```ts
// client.ts (in page)
await RedwoodClient.create({ apiKey: token }).fetch('/proxy', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) });

// service-worker.ts
self.addEventListener('fetch', (ev) => {
  if (new URL(ev.request.url).pathname === '/api/proxy') {
    ev.respondWith(fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', {
      method: ev.request.method,
      headers: ev.request.headers, // proxying headers through SW
      body: ev.request.body,
      mode: 'cors',
      credentials: 'include'
    }));
  }
});
```

jess: SDK version used by customer: ts-sdk 0.8.3, bundler: Vercel edge (esbuild), runtime: edge. They only see this in Safari. Chrome/Firefox OK.

oliver (eng-runtime): Two quick things: 1) Browser requires the Access-Control-Allow-Headers response to include "Authorization" for the preflight to succeed. 2) If the SW or Vercel edge returns an opaque or opaque-redirect response to the OPTIONS request, Safari behaves stricter and may still block. Do we see the preflight hitting our backend or does Vercel handle it?

jess: Customer captured network trace. OPTIONS goes to /api/proxy (so SW handles it) and the SW forwards it to our API. Our API responds 200 but response headers are missing Access-Control-Allow-Headers and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. Network log:

```
OPTIONS https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 200
Request headers: Origin: https://customer.app, Access-Control-Request-Method: POST, Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type
Response headers: content-type: application/json, cache-control: no-store
(---- missing: Access-Control-Allow-Headers, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials ----)
```

jess: Safari console: "Request header field Authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers." Then the POST happens and our API returns 403 because no auth header was sent.

sam (devex): That lines up: the preflight isn't being augmented with CORS response headers. two likely culprits: (A) our runtime's cors middleware never ran for OPTIONS because the SW forwarded the raw headers object (ev.request.headers) which is a Headers object that may be non-serializable across the SW <-> fetch boundary and could drop casing/authorization; (B) Vercel edge may treat OPTIONS differently and return a default response before our app code gets it.

maya (support): Customer claims they only see this when the request path is proxied through the SW. If they call the API directly from the page (no SW) it works in Safari. So SW involvement is critical.

oliver (eng-runtime): Quick experiment to ask them to try: change the SW to explicitly set the headers on the forwarded request instead of passing ev.request.headers. Eg:

```js
const headers = new Headers();
headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
headers.set('Authorization', ev.request.headers.get('Authorization') || '');
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', { method: ev.request.method, headers, body: await ev.request.clone().text(), mode: 'cors', credentials: 'include' });
```

If that fixes it, the problem is that the Headers object crossing contexts drops the Authorization entry in Safari/Vercel.

jess: Sent the suggested patch to customer. They tested and confirm: explicitly copying headers makes the OPTIONS include Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization and the response now has Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization and the POST goes through.

sam (devex): Good repro. Two follow-ups: 1) Recommend a short-term doc note for customers using service workers: don't proxy raw ev.request.headers; copy important headers. 2) Longer term: investigate whether our http handler can add Access-Control-Allow-Headers even when the request lacks them (safest path for hosted API). But we need to be careful to not expose headers to unexpected origins.

oliver (eng-runtime): I'll add a quick test in our edge runtime suite to simulate a worker proxying Headers across and confirm behavior in the Vercel-compatible harness. If it's a Vercel quirk we can document it. If it's our SDK wrapper serializing headers weirdly, we'll patch.

jess: Customer also mentioned they tried upgrading the SDK to 0.9.0 but still saw the issue until they changed header copying. So seems unrelated to SDK logic. Marking as customer-blocker resolved-on-customer-side for now.

maya (support): I'll send the customer a runbook: explanation, the explicit header copy snippet, and a short workaround: avoid proxying Authorization via service worker unless you explicitly set Access-Control-Allow-* headers on the response or copy headers manually.

ops-bot: deploy status: test-suite/job-edge-headers passed on main (sanity test added) :white_check_mark:

sam (devex): Filing a tiny docs issue for "Edge service-worker proxying and CORS" and adding a note to the TS SDK troubleshooting guide referencing this thread.

jess: Thanks team. I put the customer's app logs in the ticket and noted the workaround they applied. Closing internal thread, keeping customer ticket open until they confirm production roll. :thumbsup:
